newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen falling as Kia impacts continue.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen falling as Kia impacts continue.

text.p: Stocks were to fall on Monday as troubles at the Kia Group would continue to create a bottleneck in financial markets, brokers said.
"Investors remain skittish as the Kia problems show no signs of resolution," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
The composite stock index ended 1.32 points lower at 732.32 on Saturday.

Brokers said the market's depression was reflected in falling customer deposits with securities houses, which stood at 3.06 trillion won on Friday, compared with a yearly high of 3.59 trillion won in mid-June.
"If the deposits drop below three trillion won, the index would test the 700 level as a bottom," said Kwon Oh-soon, a broker at Hannuri Salomon Securities.
Brokers said investors would hold out their investment decisions until Wednesday when creditor banks were scheduled to meet to work out details of a rescue plan for the troubled Kia Group.
Most shares, except some theme-backed shares, would continue to fall, they said.
